I am 78 now, and my legs ache when the weather turns. It is just my husband and me in the house, so we cannot do the heavy work we once could. But I have farmed these plots for 35 years, and I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. Seven mu go to the wheat-maize rotation—that is our bread and butter, reliable and familiar. The remaining 3.1 mu I plant with cotton because the price is good, but I keep it small because picking cotton by hand at my age is backbreaking.

The wheat went into the ground last October, and now it is waking up. I will topdress it with compound fertilizer broadcast by hand when it greens up in March, and I will irrigate it three times from our well: at jointing, at heading, and once more when the grains are filling. I use my own saved seed—an improved variety I have kept for years—and I rotary till the soil before sowing each autumn. For sprays, I will do two rounds for insects, one for weeds, and one for fungus. If the frost stays away, I expect about 550 kg per mu.

As soon as the wheat comes off around June 1st, I will sow the summer maize without ploughing—just clear the stubble and plant. I buy hybrid Denghai 605 seed from the county supply store; it is vigorous and saves me trouble. I spread compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice during the summer, since the rains usually help. Maize needs two insecticide sprays and one herbicide spray. I hope for about 577 kg per mu.

For cotton, I rotary till in early spring and sow in mid-March with improved seed I buy from the store. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate once during flowering. Cotton is greedy for sprays—aphids and mites are relentless—so I will spray ten times for insects, plus once for weeds and once for fungus. I expect about 275 kg of seed cotton per mu. At my age, that is all the cotton I can manage.

I do not bother with straight fertilizers anymore; the compound bags from the supply store are easier on my memory. And because we pump from a well, I am careful with water—I only irrigate when the leaves start to curl.
